A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable algorithms, equations, tables, and complete Appendices A–Q. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Appendix A reports original gradient-descent experiments on two analytic functions, including convergence counts and divergence observations.

after.justification: Appendix A retains those original experiments and adds objective-gap trajectories in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same GD and minibatch SGD updates and integral step-size rules. The added SciPy example and explicit i.i.d. sampling annotation document procedures already described or assumed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two functions, -log(x)-log(0.1-x) and exp(x)+exp(1-x), in Appendix A. No additional dataset, task, or experimental scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Appendix A retains Li et al. (2024a) and Vankov et al. (2024) in the first comparison, and the same alternative smoothness choices and Li step size in the second. Figures 2–3 introduce no additional comparator.

E3.justification: The experiments retain the objective-gap threshold of 10^-5, the first problem's starting point of 10^-7, and the same smoothness functions and step sizes. No revised experimental protocol is documented.

E4.justification: Both versions use the same toy experiments to examine adaptive step sizes and the choice of smoothness exponent. The added plots visualize these existing comparisons without introducing another ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical high-probability analysis is retained.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 newly report per-iteration objective gaps; v1 supplied only convergence summaries. Those summaries remain unchanged, although Figure 2 appears to reach 10^-5 near 60 iterations while the prose still states 75, so the curve does not establish a verified performance improvement.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Eq. (10) from a squared-gradient bound to a gradient-norm bound, revises Lemma I.1's domain and admissible step range, and changes the stochastic gradient-cost expression from Θ(rBT) to Θ(BT). Appendix K replaces an intermediate max with min, adds case reasoning, and changes a prefactor from 4 to 16, although Section 7.2 retains 4. These are local revisions to the existing theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same integral step-size proposal, convex and nonconvex convergence claims, stochastic extension, and empirical-verification claim.

C2.justification: The discussion after Theorem 7.2 correctly describes its convergence bound as implicit, replacing 'explicit' after v1's Theorem 9.2. The existing bounded-gradient qualifications and light-tail limitation remain.

D1.justification: Figure 1 adds a concrete SciPy integrate.quad implementation of the existing step-size integral, beyond v1's general suggestion to use numerical quadrature. Algorithm 2 also explicitly identifies samples as i.i.d., already assumed in Appendix P.

R1.justification: V2 adds Xie et al. (2024) on online learning, Cooper (2024) on smoothness in deep learning, and Virtanen et al. (2020) for SciPy. The principal novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes related work and contributions into Introduction subsections, places contributions before motivating examples, and renames several headings. It also makes local language edits and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement; most prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the code example in Figure 1 and convergence plots in Figures 2–3. Table 2 displays the existing Eq. (17) formula instead of merely referencing it, and table styling, algorithm placement, and surrounding layout are adjusted.

improvement.justification: The Eq. (10) correction and revised Appendix I/K reasoning improve mathematical precision, while the SciPy example and plots aid inspection. The net gain is limited by unresolved consistency issues: Appendix K uses 16 where Section 7.2 retains 4, and Figure 2 is not fully reconciled with the 75-iteration statement.
